citation.title: Skill Scores Based on the Mean Square Error and Their Relationships to the Correlation Coefficient

topic: MSE-based skill scores relative to reference forecasts; decomposition into squared correlation, conditional bias, unconditional bias
own_question: How do MSE skill scores under internal/external, single/multiple-valued climatological references relate to the correlation coefficient, and what does correlation miss?
actual_method_and_evidence: Analytical decomposition (Eqs. 9-15) plus numerical illustration on operational NWS PoP and minimum-temperature forecasts for Portland, Oregon, warm seasons 1980-85 (Tables 1-3). No fusion or plasma content.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: An MSE skill score can be defined relative to a reference forecast. It equals 1 minus the ratio of forecast MSE to reference MSE. Its value depends on which reference is chosen. This supports reporting skill against stated baselines such as hold, causal GP or interpolation.
claim_checks.original_pdf_locator: p.2418 Eqs.(2)-(3); p.2419 Eqs.(4)-(7); p.2423 discussion of Table 2
claim_checks.qualification: Murphy's references are climatological. Using hold, causal GP or interpolation as references is our extension, not his.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Squared correlation measures potential skill. Actual MSE skill is lower by nonnegative conditional-bias and unconditional-bias terms. Correlation alone can therefore overstate performance.
claim_checks.qualification: The exact identity holds for the internal single-valued reference (Case I). Murphy's numerical magnitudes are meteorological and do not transfer to CES nowcasting.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not applicable; the forecasts are meteorological, with no diagnostic-arrival timing.
validation_if_relevant: Uses in-sample operational verification only; no train/test split. It does not inform our four validation designs.
forbidden_inferences: Do not claim that Murphy addressed plasma, CES, BES/ECEI or nowcasting.
Do not transfer the 1-13% or up to 50% gap numbers to our work.
Do not present the decomposition as evidence that our estimators perform well.
Do not treat CES labels as truth because skill scores are used.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Include in the theory and metrics background. It justifies reporting baseline-relative MSE skill together with bias terms rather than correlation alone.
